static.dataset: Ward → Westminster constituency → LAD lookup (July 2024 vintage)
static.note: 650 constituencies, 8,396 wards. Known limitation: 390 wards nationally (4.6%) are flagged by ONS as split across 2+ constituencies; this project assigns each to a single constituency rather than proportionally splitting it, so a constituency containing one of these wards may be missing that ward's local election results entirely, or crediting itself with results that partly belong to a neighbouring seat. A proper fix needs population-weighted boundary geometry (see docs/senedd_crosswalk.md for the same technique applied to a different problem), not attempted here.
One CSV per council per year — see the per-row "source"/"csv" links on each constituency page for the exact file behind any given number.

static.source_name: UK Parliament / House of Commons Library official results database
static.note: 4,515 candidate rows, all 650 constituencies. Per-constituency source links are on each seat's GE2024 section.

mrp_releases.methodology_notes: MRP fielded by Focaldata, commissioned/published by Best for Britain. Uses the NEW (2023 boundary review) constituencies, the same ones that became GE2024's — the oldest release in this dataset on compatible boundaries. GB only (no NI). Only the 'Baseline MRP' scenario loaded; the source also has Reform-UK-stands-down and don't-know-reallocation scenarios, not loaded. Source is PDF-only (no CSV/xlsx) — extracted via scripts/prep_bestforbritain_pdf.py with pdfplumber, which hit real PDF text-wrap corruption (see docs/data_notes.md); 584 of 632 possible seats passed validation (fuzzy name match + plausible vote-share sum + no ambiguous collisions) and were loaded, 48 were rejected rather than risk silently wrong numbers. NOTE: unlike every other release here, this source's own published tables list only the parties it explicitly modelled per seat (typically the top 4-6) with no residual 'Other'/minor-party catch-all column — so its per-seat shares genuinely sum to well under 100% (usually 75-90%), by design of the source, not a loading error.

MRP using Ipsos UK KnowledgePanel (random probability address-based sampling). GB only. Published 16 days before the actual GE2024 (4 Jul 2024) — one of the closest-to-election projections in this dataset. Source file also has confidence intervals and a strong/likely/lean/toss-up classification per seat, not loaded (schema only stores a point estimate).

MRP, YouGov's final call ahead of GE2024 (published day before the 4 Jul 2024 election). GB only. Exact fieldwork dates and sample size not disclosed on the source page. Source file also carries the actual GE2024 winner/runner-up per seat (added after the fact for YouGov's own retrospective piece) — not loaded, since we already have the real result from the official source (08_ingest_ge2024_results.py).

MRP, published on GE2024 polling day itself (4 Jul 2024), with fieldwork running right up to the evening before. GB only. n=36,350, the largest sample of the releases loaded so far. Source file includes a win-probability per party per seat, loaded into win_probability_pct.

MRP, titled 'More in Common's April MRP'. GB only. Exact fieldwork dates not stated on the source page (sample size 'over 16,000' also approximate). Post-stratification frame used 2024 census data plus More in Common's own post-election polling, since 2024 BES data wasn't yet available. Includes an explicit constituency-code column in the source file, so no fuzzy name matching was needed for this release.
MRP, titled 'More in Common's July MRP'. GB only. Key finding: projected Reform UK as largest party with 290 seats.
MRP, titled 'More in Common's September MRP'. GB only. 'Other' is a catch-all bucket.

MRP, titled 'More in Common's January MRP'. GB only. 'Other' is a catch-all bucket, not a single party. Note from the authors: this is a snapshot, not a projection, given 3.5 years remained before the next GE was due.

MRP; fieldwork 1-8 Dec 2025, fielded via Find Out Now. GB only (no NI seats). Loaded the 'No TV' (raw model) scenario. SNP/Plaid split by nation. Has a 'YP' party column not seen in later releases; no 'Restore' column yet. The source file also has a 'Q3. Top Three Cost-of-living Issues' section (Energy/Food/Tax/etc.) sharing the same header row — correctly excluded, not party data.
MRP, titled 'More in Common's April MRP'. GB only. 'Other' is a catch-all bucket, not a single party.

MRP; fieldwork 27 Mar-7 Apr 2026, fielded via Find Out Now's panel. GB only (no NI seats). Loaded the 'No TV' (raw model) scenario. SNP/Plaid split by nation. No separate 'Restore' column in this release (Restore Britain wasn't yet broken out as its own line).

MRP; fieldwork 23-30 Jun 2026. GB only (no NI seats). Loaded the 'No TV' (raw model, before tactical-voting adjustment) scenario — EC also publishes a tactically-adjusted 'With TV' variant, not loaded. SNP/Plaid published as one combined column, split here by constituency nation. 'Minor Party' and 'Indep/Other' are catch-all buckets, not single parties.

MRP, titled 'The Final MRP of Keir Starmer's Premiership'. GB only. Does not factor in recent by-election results, but does include English local elections and Scottish/Welsh Parliament results. 'Other' is a catch-all bucket, not a single party.
